question: Which property is shown by ALL living organisms without exception?
why: Reproduction fails in a sterile mule and growth stops in adults; metabolism is the defining feature of every living thing.

question: Which taxonomic category is placed immediately above family?
why: The ranks run species, genus, family, order, class, phylum, kingdom.

question: Which rule is correct for writing the scientific name Triticum aestivum?
a: Both words start with capital letters
b: Genus in small letters, species epithet starts with a capital
c: Both words in capital letters, underlined only
d: Genus starts with a capital letter, species epithet in small letters, both italicised
why: The genus name begins with a capital letter and the species epithet is all small letters; both are italicised.

question: In a taxonomic key, each single statement of a contrasting pair is called a
why: A pair of contrasting statements is a couplet; each statement in it is a lead.

question: Panthera leo, Panthera tigris and Panthera pardus share a genus. Which statement must be true?
a: They belong to the same species but different varieties
b: They also share the same family, order and class
c: They share a genus but belong to different families
d: They share a family but different orders
why: All higher ranks that contain a genus contain all its species, so a shared genus means a shared family, order and class.

question: Mangifera indica and Mangifera sylvatica are two different organisms. What do they have in common and how do they differ?
c: Same family, same genus and same species
why: The first word (genus) is shared; the second word (species epithet) separates them.

question: The cell wall of fungi is made mainly of
why: Fungal walls contain chitin; cellulose is typical of plants and peptidoglycan of bacteria.

question: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by
why: Whittaker proposed it in 1969.

question: Which is the smallest living cell known and can survive without oxygen?
why: Mycoplasma has no cell wall, is about 0.1 micrometre across and many types are anaerobic.

question: Red tides in the sea are caused by rapid multiplication of
why: Gonyaulax and other dinoflagellates bloom and colour the water red, releasing toxins.

question: Which statement about viruses is correct?
a: Each virus has either DNA or RNA as genetic material, never both
b: Viroids have a protein coat around their RNA
c: Prions are infectious particles with RNA but no protein
why: Viroids are free RNA without a coat, prions are proteins and phages mostly have double-stranded DNA.

question: Alternaria and Trichoderma are placed in the class of fungi called Deuteromycetes. This is because in them
d: only the asexual conidial stage is known
why: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because the sexual phase is not known; if found they are moved to another class.

question: The brown colour of brown algae is due to the pigment
why: Fucoxanthin is the xanthophyll that masks chlorophyll in Phaeophyceae.

question: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they
c: live on land but need water for fertilisation
d: live partly in sea and partly in fresh water
why: Their male gametes swim in water to reach the egg.

question: In ferns the free-living, photosynthetic, multicellular gametophyte is called the
why: The fern gametophyte is a small heart-shaped prothallus.

question: Coralloid roots of Cycas are associated with
why: Coralloid roots host Anabaena or Nostoc, which fix nitrogen.

question: Which life cycle pattern is correctly matched?
why: Spirogyra is haplontic; Fucus is diplontic, Pinus diplontic, Funaria haplodiplontic.

question: The leaf cells of a fern sporophyte have 64 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in its spore mother cell, a spore and a prothallus cell respectively?
why: The mother cell is 2n = 64, meiosis gives haploid spores of 32 and the prothallus grows from a spore by mitosis, so it stays 32.

question: Adult echinoderms show which type of body symmetry?
why: Adult echinoderms are radial; their larvae are bilateral.

question: Which of these is a cephalochordate?
why: Branchiostoma (Amphioxus) keeps its notochord from head to tail throughout life.

question: Which pair correctly matches the animal with its body cavity?
why: Ascaris has a body cavity not lined by mesoderm; Taenia is acoelomate and Pheretima is coelomate.

question: Which animal has a closed circulatory system?
why: Annelids such as Pheretima have blood in vessels; arthropods and most molluscs have an open system.

question: Which statement is true of class Chondrichthyes?
a: Gills are covered by an operculum
c: Gill slits are separate and have no operculum
d: Skin is covered by cycloid scales
why: Sharks lack an operculum and air bladder, and have placoid scales.

question: Which animal is correctly paired with its class?
why: The platypus is an egg-laying mammal; sea horse is bony fish, Salamandra is amphibian and Pteropus (flying fox) is a mammal.

question: Which root system is found in wheat?
why: Monocots like wheat have fibrous roots replacing the short-lived radicle.

question: Pneumatophores of mangrove plants help in
why: These upward roots stick out of marshy soil to take in air.

question: Placentation in mustard is
why: Mustard has ovules on the ovary wall; axile is in China rose and marginal in pea.

question: Vexillary aestivation is shown by
why: Pea has a standard petal overlapping the wings, which overlap the keel.

question: A flower has a superior bicarpellary ovary with swollen placentae, axile placentation, five united sepals and five united petals with epipetalous stamens. The family is
why: This combination describes potato, tomato and brinjal: Solanaceae.

question: Which set of characters belongs to Fabaceae?
a: Papilionaceous corolla, diadelphous stamens, monocarpellary ovary with marginal placentation
b: Tetradynamous stamens, parietal placentation, siliqua fruit
c: Six tepals, six stamens, trilocular ovary
d: Epipetalous stamens, bicarpellary obliquely placed ovary
why: The pea family has a papilionaceous corolla, 9+1 stamens and a single carpel.

question: Companion cells are closely associated with
why: Companion cells keep the enucleate sieve tubes alive.

question: Increase in girth of a dicot stem is due to
why: Vascular cambium and cork cambium add girth.

question: Which feature is seen in a monocot stem but not in a dicot stem?
a: Vascular bundles arranged in a ring and open
why: Monocot bundles lie scattered, lack cambium and are closed.

question: Heartwood differs from sapwood because heartwood
b: is dark and no longer conducts water
d: is formed by the cork cambium
why: Heartwood is filled with tannins and resins and is non-conducting.

question: A leaf section shows undifferentiated mesophyll, bulliform cells and stomata on both surfaces. It is most likely a leaf of
why: Isobilateral leaves with bulliform cells are typical of monocot grasses like maize.

question: Cork cambium produces
b: secondary xylem inward and phloem outward
why: Phellogen cuts cork outward and secondary cortex inward; the three form the periderm.

question: Which epithelium lines blood vessels and alveoli?
why: Thin flat cells allow quick diffusion.

question: Tendons connect
why: Ligaments join bone to bone.

question: A cockroach has how many pairs of spiracles?
why: Two thoracic and eight abdominal pairs.

question: Which cell junction allows rapid transfer of ions and small molecules between neighbouring animal cells?
why: Gap junctions connect cytoplasm of adjoining cells; plasmodesmata are plant structures.

question: In a frog, blood from the sinus venosus first enters the
why: The sinus venosus opens into the right atrium of the three-chambered heart.

question: Which gives the correct segment numbers in Pheretima: clitellum, female genital pore, male genital pore?
why: The clitellum covers segments 14 to 16, the single female pore is on the 14th and male pores are on the 18th.

question: Which organelle is the main site of ATP production in aerobic respiration?
why: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell.

question: The prokaryotic ribosome has a sedimentation coefficient of
why: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits.

question: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by
why: They proposed it in 1972.

question: A centriole shows which arrangement of microtubules?
a: nine doublets with two central tubules
b: nine singlets with one central tubule
d: nine peripheral triplets, no central tubule
why: Cilia have 9+2 doublets; centrioles are 9+0 triplets.

question: The sodium-potassium pump
a: moves Na+ in and K+ out down gradients without energy
b: moves both ions in by facilitated diffusion
c: moves Na+ out and K+ in against gradients using ATP
why: It is an active transport protein that keeps ion gradients.

question: Which pair of organelles are semi-autonomous, having their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes?
why: Both are thought to have arisen from endosymbiotic prokaryotes.

question: A peptide bond links
b: the carboxyl group of one amino acid to the amino group of the next
why: Peptide bonds are formed with loss of water between COOH and NH2.

question: Most enzymes are
why: Some catalytic RNA exist, but nearly all enzymes are proteins.

question: The Michaelis constant (Km) is the substrate concentration at which the reaction velocity is
why: Km is a measure of affinity of enzyme for substrate.

question: Malonate inhibits succinate dehydrogenase because it
a: binds irreversibly to a distant site
c: resembles the substrate and competes for the active site
why: Structural similarity makes it a competitive inhibitor.

question: A competitive inhibitor added to an enzyme reaction will
b: raise Km and leave Vmax unchanged
c: leave Km unchanged and lower Vmax
d: lower Km and leave Vmax unchanged
why: More substrate can outcompete the inhibitor, so Vmax is unchanged but more substrate is needed to reach half Vmax.

question: A DNA fragment has 20 A-T base pairs and 30 G-C base pairs. Its total number of hydrogen bonds is
why: A-T pairs have 2 bonds and G-C pairs 3: 40 + 90 = 130.

question: DNA replication occurs in which phase of the cell cycle?
why: Synthesis phase doubles the DNA content.

question: Chromosomes line up at the equator of the cell during
why: Spindle fibres align chromosomes at the metaphase plate.

question: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids takes place during
why: Recombination nodules form at pachytene.

question: The synaptonemal complex is formed during
why: Synapsis of homologous chromosomes begins at zygotene.

question: A diploid cell has 2n = 12. How many bivalents form at metaphase I, and how many chromosomes does each cell have at the end of meiosis II?
why: Twelve chromosomes pair into 6 bivalents; meiosis halves the number to 6.

question: A cell has 2C DNA in G1. What is the DNA amount per cell at the end of meiosis I and at the end of meiosis II respectively?
why: S phase makes 4C; meiosis I halves it to 2C per cell and meiosis II to C.

question: The light reactions of photosynthesis occur in the
why: Pigments and electron carriers lie in the grana thylakoids.

question: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in C3 plants is
why: RuBisCO adds CO2 to RuBP giving two molecules of 3-PGA.

question: The primary CO2 acceptor in C4 plants is
why: PEP carboxylase in mesophyll cells fixes CO2 to make OAA.

question: Photolysis of water is associated with
why: PS II (P680) splits water to supply electrons and release oxygen.

question: To make one glucose by the C3 cycle and by the C4 pathway, the ATP needed is respectively
why: C3 needs 3 ATP per CO2; C4 needs 5.

question: In photorespiration the organelles involved in order are
why: RuBP oxygenation starts in the chloroplast; glycolate moves to peroxisome then mitochondrion.

question: Glycolysis takes place in the
why: It breaks down glucose to pyruvate outside organelles.

question: The final electron acceptor in the mitochondrial electron transport chain is
why: Oxygen accepts electrons and protons to form water.

question: Per glucose molecule, how many CO2 molecules are released in the link reaction and Krebs cycle together?
why: Two in link reaction plus four in two turns of the cycle.

question: The respiratory quotient when fats are the substrate is
why: Fats need more oxygen per CO2 released; the value is about 0.7.

question: Which statement about ATP synthase is correct?
a: F1 forms a proton channel and F0 has the catalytic site
c: F0 forms a proton channel and F1 has the catalytic site
d: It pumps protons into the matrix
why: Protons flow through F0 and drive ATP synthesis in F1.

question: Palmitic acid is oxidised as C16H32O2 + 23 O2 giving 16 CO2 + 16 H2O. Its RQ is about
why: 16 divided by 23 is 0.70.

question: Which plant hormone is a gas?
why: Ethylene promotes fruit ripening.

question: Which hormone promotes cell elongation in stems?
why: Auxins promote elongation and apical dominance.

question: Bolting in rosette plants such as cabbage is induced by
why: Gibberellins elongate the internodes.

question: Which hormone delays senescence of leaves?
why: Cytokinins help to keep leaves green and promote cell division.

question: A short-day plant receives long nights. A brief flash of red light is given in the middle of the dark period. The plant will
why: Flowering depends on an unbroken dark period; red light converts Pr to Pfr and breaks the night.

question: A tissue grows exponentially with relative growth rate r. Its size W1 after time t is
why: Exponential growth multiplies the starting size W0 by e raised to rt.

question: During normal inspiration the diaphragm
why: Contraction increases the volume of the thoracic cavity.

question: The tidal volume of a healthy adult is about
why: About 6000 to 8000 mL of air is moved per minute.

question: A person has tidal volume 500 mL, inspiratory reserve volume 2500 mL and expiratory reserve volume 1000 mL. The vital capacity is
The expiratory reserve volume is 1100 mL and the residual volume is 1200 mL. The functional residual capacity is
why: FRC = ERV + RV.

question: The oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve shifts to the right in actively metabolising tissues because of
a: high pCO2, high H+ and higher temperature
b: low pCO2, low H+ and lower temperature
why: These factors lower haemoglobin affinity for oxygen, helping unloading.

question: Chloride shift in red blood cells is the movement of
a: Cl- out of RBC as HCO3- moves in
d: Cl- into RBC as HCO3- moves out
why: It maintains ionic balance while carbon dioxide is carried as bicarbonate.

question: Which blood group has no antigens on its red cells?
why: Group O RBCs have neither A nor B antigen.

question: Normal blood pressure of a healthy adult is about
why: Systolic over diastolic.

question: A person with blood group A has which antibodies in plasma?
why: Plasma contains antibodies against the antigen the person lacks.

question: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur when the
a: mother is Rh-negative and the foetus is Rh-positive
b: mother is Rh-positive and the foetus is Rh-negative
why: The mother makes anti-Rh antibodies that attack a later Rh-positive foetus.

question: The end of the T-wave in an ECG marks
c: the start of the cardiac cycle
why: The T wave is ventricular repolarisation, returning the ventricles to the resting state.

question: A heart pumps 60 mL per beat at 75 beats per minute. Cardiac output per minute is
why: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate = 60 x 75.

question: The functional unit of the kidney is the
why: Each kidney has about a million nephrons.

question: The chief nitrogenous waste of human beings is
why: The liver converts ammonia to urea.

question: The glomerular filtration rate of a healthy adult is about
why: This is about 180 litres per day.

question: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is
a: impermeable to water, permeable to electrolytes
d: permeable to water, almost impermeable to electrolytes
why: The ascending limb is the opposite; this sets up the medullary gradient.

question: Atrial natriuretic factor acts on the kidney by
c: causing vasodilation and countering the RAAS
why: ANF lowers blood pressure and opposes the renin-angiotensin mechanism.

question: Cortical nephrons differ from juxtamedullary nephrons in that cortical nephrons have
a: a long loop of Henle and well-developed vasa recta
b: a short loop of Henle and reduced vasa recta
why: Juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops that help concentrate urine.

question: The adult human skeleton has how many bones?
why: Babies have more bones that fuse.

question: The contractile proteins of muscle are
why: Thin actin and thick myosin filaments slide over each other.

question: Movement in all directions is possible at a
why: The shoulder is the common example.

question: Binding of Ca2+ to which protein exposes the myosin-binding sites on actin?
why: Ca2+ binds troponin, which shifts tropomyosin away.

question: During muscle contraction the length of which band remains unchanged?
why: Myosin filaments stay the same length; the I band and H zone narrow.

question: An autoimmune disorder that affects the neuromuscular junction, causing fatigue and weakness, is
why: Antibodies block receptors at the junction.

question: The brain part that controls balance and posture is the
why: The cerebellum coordinates movement.

question: The part of a neuron that receives signals is the
why: Dendrites carry impulses toward the cell body.

question: A resting axon membrane is more permeable to
why: Potassium leaks out, leaving the outside positively charged.

question: In myelinated fibres the impulse jumps from node to node. This is
why: Myelin insulates the fibre, so impulses are faster.

question: Which sequence describes an action potential?
a: Na+ influx, K+ efflux, then restoring by the sodium-potassium pump
b: K+ influx, Na+ efflux, then diffusion
c: Ca2+ influx, Cl- efflux, then osmosis
d: K+ efflux, Na+ influx, then phagocytosis
why: Depolarisation by Na+ entry, repolarisation by K+ exit, and the pump resets ions.

question: Sound waves reach the cochlear fluid by passing through
a: oval window, stapes, incus, malleus, tympanum
d: tympanic membrane, malleus, incus, stapes, oval window
why: The ossicles amplify the vibrations to the oval window.

question: The master gland of the body is the
why: It controls many other endocrine glands.

question: Insulin is secreted by
c: beta cells of the islets of Langerhans
why: Beta cells make insulin; alpha cells make glucagon.

question: Deficiency of dietary iodine causes
why: Low thyroxine causes the thyroid to enlarge.

question: Over-secretion of growth hormone in an adult causes
why: In children excess GH causes gigantism; in adults the bones of hands and face thicken.

question: Which hormone acts mainly through intracellular receptors?
why: Steroid hormones diffuse in and act on gene expression; peptides and amines act on surface receptors.

question: A patient shows weakness, low blood pressure, low blood sodium and darker skin. The likely cause is
why: This is Addison disease.
